GENERATE BURST T10K-A2 — Run C-9 Phase 2, T10 the Frost King's Barrow (Matt R-C9-73: a fully generated pipeline): MODEL SHEET for 3D assets, painted as ALBEDO. task_id "T10K-A2".

**Why this sheet exists.** A 3D model is built from these four views, placed in a snowbound
level, and **lit there by a real sun**. The world is being built the way the character was
built, so the same two things decide whether the sheet works.

**One object in four views, not four objects.** The same silhouette, the same stone, the
same carving, the same every mark, seen from four sides. The two profiles are each other's
mirror — that is the one constraint a drawing cannot fake and a multiview build cannot
recover from.

**Paint the surface, not the lighting.** Soft, even, shadowless light from nowhere in
particular. No key, no bright side and dark side, no rim light, no cast shadow, no shadow
on the ground, no ambient dark gathering in the cracks. Tone comes from the object's own
colours and from the pen hatching. Light that is painted in happens twice when the engine
lights it — that is the whole finding of T9.

**SNOW IS PAINTED AS SURFACE COLOUR, NOT AS LIGHT.** Where the concept shows a cap of snow
on a stone or a rock, paint it: cream-white, granular, with its own soft edge and the pen
line around it. It is the object's albedo, the same as its lichen. A shader adds snow to
upward faces on top of this, so paint what is *there*, not what the sun does to it.

**SHEET.** Flat pure #00ff00, nothing else. The four views of one object at exactly the
same scale, on one ground line, each filling most of its cell. Columns left to right:
**FRONT**, **RIGHT SIDE** (profile, facing the viewer's right), **BACK**, **LEFT SIDE**.
No ground, no shadow, no text, no labels, no cell borders, no other objects, nothing
overlapping.

**STYLE:** the REGISTER CARD governs line, washes, light and plate; its manuscript-subject
clause does not apply. Paint in IMAGE 2's hand (`inputs/nb_style_ref_matt.png`) — the same
hand the barbarian is painted in.

---

**Sheet:** 1536×1024 landscape, 4 columns × 2 rows. Top row the first object, bottom row the second; each row is ONE object in four views at one scale. The two rows need not share a scale.

**These are small props that dress the ground around the barrow**, seen later from above at a steep angle, so their tops and outlines matter most. Keep the stone, the snow and the washes in the colours of IMAGE 1.

**Leave a clear gap of plain background between every view and between the two rows**: no part of one view may reach into its neighbour's cell.

**PROPORTIONS ARE PART OF THE DESIGN.** Each object below states how wide it is against how high. Draw that shape; do not stretch or stack an object to fill its cell.

**TOP ROW — THREE ROCKS SET APART.** Three separate snow-capped rocks of weathered grey-green granite lying apart on one patch of ground, with bare gaps between them: one knee-high, two smaller. No rock sits on another. The group is about TWICE as wide as the tallest rock is high. Pitted faces, flecks of pale lichen, one patch of rust-orange lichen on the largest; a thin cap of wind-packed snow on each. The three rocks are ONE object: the same rocks in the same places in all four views.

**BOTTOM ROW — A LOW, BROAD BIRCH STUMP.** The stump of an old birch broken off LOW, at about a man's shin height, with thick roots running out along the ground on every side and reaching twice as far as the stump is tall, so the whole thing is about TWICE as wide as it is high. Chalk-white bark peeling in papery curls and banded with black scars; the broken top jagged; the dead wood inside grey. Snow on the broken top and between the roots.

Deliver ONE 1536x1024 landscape sheet.
BACKGROUND: keep flat pure #00ff00. If the image model returns a darker or gradient background anyway, DO NOT spend a retry on it; deliver the image (the views are cut out afterwards).

Two image_gen calls: variants a and b. ONE retry per variant only if a view is missing or has the wrong facing, an object differs between its views, a view carries a cast shadow or a strong light direction, or objects overlap — name the reason. Never retry for the background colour. Copy outputs to out/T10K-A2_a.png and out/T10K-A2_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "T10K-A2"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — the approved Barrow concept painting (T10C-barrow_a): the PLACE these objects belong to, for its palette, its stone and its snow ONLY. None of its objects is drawn on this sheet; do not copy its composition, its light or its shadows
IMAGE 2 — STYLE reference ONLY (Matt-supplied, R-C9-69): the hand the barbarian was painted in
